item.title: UAE's JustAd attracts $5 million to expand into new markets
item.description:
• UAE-based adtech startup JustAd has secured a $5 million investment from angel investor Imad Jomaa to support its expansion into new markets. The funding round's stage and the company's valuation were not disclosed.
  • Founded in 2025 by Ahmed Elsayed, JustAd operates an AI-powered marketing platform that enables businesses and agencies to manage, track and analyse advertising campaigns.
  • The company also offers Advertise Now, Pay Later (ANPL), an embedded financing solution that allows businesses to run advertising campaigns immediately and pay for their media spending in instalments.
  • The investment will support JustAd's international expansion, including building local sales and customer support teams, adapting its platform to new markets and strengthening partnerships with major advertising platforms.
  • Having established its presence in the MENA region, JustAd plans to begin onboarding customers in its first new markets in early 2027.

Press release:

JustAd, the AI-powered marketing OS, today announced a $5 million investment from angel investor Imad Jomaa. The company will use the funding to expand quickly into new markets.

JustAd is a marketing OS: everything marketers need in one place. Teams plan, run and measure their advertising across Meta, TikTok, Snapchat and Google Ads. The platform combines AI-driven campaign analysis with tracking and attribution, product catalogue tools and unified reporting. Advertisers see what is working across every channel and can act on it without switching between tools.

JustAd is also the company that invented Advertise Now, Pay Later (ANPL), a financing model built for advertising. With ANPL, a business launches its campaigns today and pays for the media spend later, in installments of up to 12 months. Clients run on certified agency ad accounts across Meta, TikTok, Snapchat and Google Ads, with direct technical support.

The model removes one of the biggest barriers to growth for small and mid-sized advertisers: cash flow. Ad platforms charge as the budget is spent, while the revenue from those ads arrives weeks or months later. Declined or blocked cards pause campaigns and hurt performance. ANPL closes that gap, so a business can scale the campaigns that are working instead of waiting for cash to catch up.

ANPL makes JustAd the first fintech for advertisers: one platform where a business can manage, measure and finance its advertising.

The company built its base in the Middle East and North Africa, working with e-commerce brands, agencies and in-house marketing teams. The new investment takes that model into new markets.

JustAd will use the capital to build local sales and customer success teams in each new market, adapt the product locally, deepen its partnerships with the major ad platforms, and bring Advertise Now, Pay Later to advertisers there.

"Advertising is changing faster than most businesses can follow. AI is taking over how campaigns are built and measured, and budgets are spreading across more platforms every year," said Ahmed Elsayed, Founder and CEO of JustAd.

"We built JustAd by reading where the market is heading and filling the gaps before anyone else sees them. That is how we arrived at Advertise Now, Pay Later, and it is how we will keep building. The next decade of advertising belongs to the companies that give advertisers intelligence and capital in the same place. This investment lets us bring that to new markets, and Imad's backing is a strong vote of confidence in our team."

"JustAd is solving two problems every advertiser has: knowing what works and having the cash to scale it," said Imad Jomaa. "Advertise Now, Pay Later is a new idea that changes how businesses fund their growth, and Ahmed and his team have proven it in demanding markets. I am investing because I believe this model works anywhere businesses advertise. Taking it into new markets is the natural next step."

JustAd plans to begin onboarding customers in its first new markets in early 2027.

item.title: Foodics invests in Funding Souq to expand restaurant financing in KSA, UAE
item.description:
• Saudi Arabia-based fintech Funding Souq has secured a strategic investment from Foodics, making it a major investor in this round. The investment amount and ownership stake were not disclosed.
  • Founded in 2020 by Martin Jaouni, Funding Souq operates a Shariah-compliant SME financing platform regulated by the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) and the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA), offering business loans, invoice financing and supplier financing in Saudi Arabia and the UAE.
  • The partnership will enable Funding Souq to provide embedded financing to Foodics' network of restaurant and hospitality businesses, using sales and operational data to assess creditworthiness and tailor financing to merchants' needs.
  • Funding Souq claims to have attracted more than 10,000 investors to its platform and aims to facilitate $1 billion in SME financing over the next three years.

Press release:

Funding Souq, a Saudi-based Shariah-compliant crowdfunding and SME financing platform regulated by the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) and the Dubai Financial Services Authority  (DFSA), today announced a strategic investment from Foodics, the leading restaurant operations and financial technology platform in MENA, making Foodics a major investor in this round. The investment will support Funding Souq’s continued growth and expand embedded financing opportunities for SMEs.

The investment brings together Funding Souq’s regulated financing infrastructure and expertise in SME credit with Foodics’ technology and data capabilities, supporting Funding Souq’s broader growth while creating new opportunities for embedded financing. Within the F&B sector, the collaboration will enable Funding Souq to extend its financing solutions to Foodics’ network of tech-enabled restaurant merchants, using restaurant sales and performance data to support more informed credit assessment and financing better aligned with how these businesses operate.

The investment brings together Funding Souq’s regulated financing infrastructure and SME credit expertise with Foodics’ technology and extensive market reach. Within the restaurant and hospitality sector, Funding Souq will extend its financing solutions to Foodics’ customer network, using restaurant sales and performance data to assess creditworthiness and offer financing better suited to their operating needs.

This also comes as Foodics expands its financial services offering through Capital 2.0, its automated financing solution for restaurants. The company intends to deploy USD 100 million in financing through Capital 2.0 in its first year, with the launch and investment reflecting its broader push to embed access to capital within its restaurant technology ecosystem.

Martin Jaouni, Founder and CEO of Funding Souq, said, "We're delighted to partner with Foodics. Together we have created Saudi Arabia's first fully automated business loan, bringing Foodics' deep reach across the restaurant and hospitality sector together with our regulated financing infrastructure to deliver capital to merchants the moment they need it. It also marks an important acceleration of our embedded finance journey, one we intend to extend across every sector where SMEs are underserved, in both Saudi Arabia and the UAE.”

Anas AlGhanim, VP, Investments & Corporate Development at Foodics, said, "Funding Souq has built a strong financing platform with significant potential to scale and serve a broader segment of SMEs. We see this investment as an opportunity to support the company’s next phase of growth while also bringing together Funding Souq’s financing capabilities and Foodics’ technology ecosystem to expand financing services and make access to capital more seamless for our customers.”

The investment also forms part of Foodics’ longer-term ambition to evolve beyond restaurant technology into a broader financial services platform, with the company ultimately aspiring to become the future bank for restaurants and the hospitality sector. 

Funding Souq has built a community of more than 10,000 investors on its platform and is on track to facilitate USD 1 billion in financing for SMEs over the next three years, as it continues to scale its Shariah-compliant financing offering.

item.title: Syrian healthtech Alo Hakeem raises $165,000 pre-seed led by EBLA Ventures
item.description:
• Syrian healthtech startup Alo Hakeem has raised $165,000 in a pre-seed funding round led by EBLA Ventures, with participation from other undisclosed investors.
  • Founded in 2025 by Abdullatif Al-Baroudi and Albaraa Abdulsalam, Alo Hakeem operates a digital platform connecting patients with licensed home healthcare providers, offering services including medical consultations, nursing, physiotherapy, elderly care, laboratory testing and diagnostic imaging.
  • The Aleppo-based startup currently operates in Aleppo, Damascus and Hama, with plans to expand into four additional Syrian governorates by the end of 2027.
  • The funding will support the development of its technology infrastructure, expansion of its healthcare provider network and team, and the transition from its minimum viable product (MVP) to a full mobile application scheduled for public launch in November 2026.

Press release:

Syrian healthtech startup Alo Hakeem has closed a $165,000 Pre-Seed funding round led by EBLA Ventures as it prepares to launch its mobile application and expand access to home healthcare services across Syria.

The company did not disclose the identities of other participating investors or its valuation.

Founded in 2025 by Abdullatif Al-Baroudi and Albaraa Abdulsalam, Alo Hakeem operates a digital platform connecting patients and families with licensed healthcare professionals who provide medical services at home.

The startup aims to address challenges facing patients seeking reliable home healthcare while providing healthcare professionals with a more structured system for delivering services.

Its offerings include home medical consultations, nursing, physiotherapy, elderly care, laboratory testing and diagnostic imaging. The platform coordinates appointments and connects patients with healthcare providers through its website and customer support operations.

Headquartered in Aleppo, Alo Hakeem currently serves patients in Aleppo, Damascus and Hama, with plans to enter four additional Syrian governorates by the end of 2027.

The company initially financed its operations independently, developing a minimum viable product and testing its service model through direct engagement with patients and medical professionals.

During its early development, Alo Hakeem participated in the ScaleUp 2025 programme and received mentorship through ChangeMakers, a programme run by Maynger Ventures, and Thimar, an initiative supporting Syrian startups in preparing for investment.

According to the company, the new funding will support its transition from the MVP stage to a fully developed digital platform, with the official Alo Hakeem mobile application scheduled to launch publicly in November 2026.

The investment will also be used to strengthen its technology infrastructure, expand its network of licensed healthcare providers and develop its team as it enters new markets within Syria.

EBLA Ventures, which invests in and supports Syrian entrepreneurs, has worked with the startup during its early development and investment preparation.

The funding comes as technology startups seek to address gaps in Syria's healthcare system, particularly access to services outside hospitals and traditional medical facilities.

For Alo Hakeem, the next stage will centre on moving beyond its initial service model and building a platform capable of coordinating home healthcare across a wider geographical area.

item.title: Salehli raises $100,000 to expand home maintenance services in Syria
item.description:
• Syrian home maintenance services startup Salehli has secured a $100,000 investment from EBLA Ventures, marking the investment firm's fourth deal in 2026. The funding round's stage and any participation by other investors were not disclosed.
  • Founded in 2025 by AbdulRhman Arnaout, Salehli operates a digital marketplace connecting customers with pre-vetted maintenance and renovation professionals, allowing users to request services, receive quotations and access on-site quality supervision.
  • The investment follows Salehli's participation in the Thimar programme, where EBLA Ventures worked with the company's founders on business development and performance monitoring ahead of the investment.
  • The funding will support the introduction of electronic payments, expansion into B2B maintenance services and the company's entry into additional Syrian cities.

Press release:

Syrian home maintenance startup Salehli (صلّحلي) has secured a $100,000 investment from EBLA Ventures, as it prepares to expand its digital marketplace for maintenance and renovation services into new cities across Syria.

The investment marks EBLA Ventures' fourth transaction in 2026. The funding stage and any participation by other investors were not disclosed.

Salehli operates a digital platform connecting households and other customers with maintenance and renovation professionals. Through the platform, customers can submit service requests and receive quotations from professionals who have undergone prior verification, while an on-site team oversees service quality.

The startup aims to bring greater transparency to a market where customers often rely on personal recommendations and informal pricing arrangements to find maintenance providers.

According to EBLA Ventures, Salehli has attracted more than 15,000 users and 3,500 service professionals in less than a year. The platform has processed over 10,000 service requests, with repeat customers accounting for nearly half of its customer base.

The investment follows a relationship established through the Thimar programme, which supports Syrian startups in developing their businesses and preparing for investment.

After the programme, Salehli's founders continued working with EBLA Ventures to strengthen the company's operations and track its performance, leading to the investment agreement.

The new capital will support the introduction of digital payment services, the development of offerings for businesses and institutions, and expansion into additional cities across Syria.

EBLA Ventures said the investment reflects its focus on companies addressing everyday consumer needs, particularly as demand for maintenance, renovation and related services develops in Syria.

item.title: MENA startup funding jumps to $1.65 billion in Q3, with Saudi Arabia taking the lead
item.description:
Startup investment across the Middle East and North Africa more than doubled in the third quarter of 2026, driven by a wave of large Saudi fintech deals that helped revive funding activity despite persistent geopolitical uncertainty. Yet the recovery remained heavily concentrated in a handful of companies and markets, raising questions about whether the momentum can extend across the wider ecosystem.

Startups across MENA raised $1.65 billion through 145 deals between July and September, up 108% from the previous quarter, while deal volume increased 39%. Despite the sharp quarterly rebound, funding remained approximately 63% below the $4.5 billion recorded during the same period last year.

The recovery gained momentum in September, when regional funding exceeded $1.1 billion, following a subdued July and an August rebound driven largely by two UAE-based companies. Saudi Arabia reclaimed the lead from the UAE, accounting for the majority of capital deployed during the quarter.

The composition of funding also showed a notable shift. Debt financing accounted for $441 million across 10 transactions, representing 26.8% of total investment, compared with almost 59% during 2025. Non-debt funding reached $1.21 billion, suggesting that the recovery was not solely dependent on credit-backed transactions.

The quarter unfolded against a challenging geopolitical backdrop, with regional military tensions, disruptions to maritime trade and volatile energy markets complicating the investment outlook. Nevertheless, several established startups managed to secure substantial financing, demonstrating continued investor appetite for businesses with the scale and growth potential to attract large commitments.

But the headline figures obscure a more uneven picture. Capital remained concentrated in fintech, Saudi Arabia and the UAE dominated the regional rankings, and male-led startups captured nearly all the funding deployed.

Fintech dominates as large funding rounds return

Fintech strengthened its position as the region's leading investment sector, attracting $1.03 billion across 35 transactions, equivalent to approximately 62% of total quarterly funding.

Mobility ranked second, raising $285 million through just two deals, followed by e-commerce, which secured $105.6 million across nine transactions.

The sector rankings highlighted the outsized influence of a handful of large funding rounds. Saudi fintech companies Barq, Tabby and Lendo alone attracted a combined $762.5 million, accounting for nearly three-quarters of the capital deployed in fintech during the quarter.

Funding by stage revealed a similarly concentrated landscape.

Early-stage startups accounted for the largest share of deal activity, with 94 companies raising $505.4 million. Later-stage startups secured $606 million across just seven transactions, reflecting renewed investor appetite for more mature businesses capable of attracting sizable funding commitments.

Another 34 startups did not disclose their funding stages, while 10 transactions were classified as debt financing.

The figures suggest that while early-stage investment remained active, a small number of established companies continued to attract a disproportionate share of available capital.

Business-to-business (B2B) startups maintained their lead, securing $876.2 million across 95 transactions. Business-to-consumer (B2C) companies followed with $506.7 million across 27 deals, while the remaining $264.1 million went to startups operating across both business models.

The gender funding gap, meanwhile, showed little sign of narrowing.

Male-led startups attracted $1.62 billion across 116 deals, representing 98.3% of all capital raised during the quarter. Startups founded by mixed-gender teams secured $15.9 million across 13 transactions, while female-led startups raised just $12.7 million through 16 deals, accounting for less than 1% of total investment.

The disparity was particularly striking given the overall recovery in funding. While capital returned to the ecosystem, the overwhelming majority flowed to male-led companies, reinforcing the persistent imbalance in access to venture capital.

Saudi Arabia reclaims the lead

Saudi Arabia emerged as MENA's largest startup funding market in the third quarter, attracting approximately $1 billion across 62 transactions and reclaiming the top position from the UAE.

The kingdom recorded a more than tenfold increase in funding from the $102 million raised in the previous quarter, largely driven by a series of large fintech transactions announced in September.

The resurgence coincided with LEAP 2026, held in Riyadh from Aug. 31 to Sept. 3, which brought together technology companies, investors and startups. However, the quarter's performance was shaped primarily by a handful of large transactions rather than an evenly distributed recovery in investment activity.

Fintech was the clear driver of Saudi Arabia's funding growth, attracting $815.8 million across 16 transactions. E-commerce ranked second with $98 million raised through five deals, followed by proptech, which secured $50.3 million across four transactions.

Three fintech transactions stood out.

Barq closed a $329.5 million Series A round at a valuation of $1.85 billion, while Tabby raised $233 million in Series F funding, valuing the buy now, pay later company at $6.5 billion. Lendo secured another $200 million through debt financing.

Together, the three transactions accounted for $762.5 million, equivalent to approximately three-quarters of the kingdom's quarterly funding and more than 90% of its fintech investment.

The concentration illustrates the growing influence of Saudi fintech companies on regional funding performance, particularly as larger businesses continue to attract capital amid a challenging investment environment.

Debt remained an important component of Saudi Arabia's funding landscape, accounting for $372 million across six transactions.

Early-stage startups nevertheless maintained a strong presence, with 34 companies raising a combined $392.7 million. Another 19 startups did not disclose their funding stages.

Saudi Arabia's performance highlighted its ability to attract sizable investment commitments despite regional uncertainty. However, the significant concentration of funding in a few fintech companies suggests that the quarter's rebound was driven more by the scale of individual transactions than a broad-based increase in investment across the ecosystem.

UAE slips to second despite strong late-stage activity

The UAE retreated to second place in the regional rankings after leading MENA startup funding during the previous quarter.

UAE-based startups raised $507 million across 41 transactions, down 14% from the $591.3 million recorded in Q2.

Despite the decline, the country continued to attract substantial later-stage investment, reinforcing its position as one of the region's most established startup funding markets.

Unlike Saudi Arabia, where fintech dominated investment, mobility emerged as the UAE's largest sector, attracting $250 million through a single transaction. Fintech ranked second with $164.3 million across 15 deals, followed by healthtech, which secured $25.2 million through three transactions.

Two later-stage funding rounds accounted for nearly 63% of the country's quarterly investment.

Mobility company Moove raised $250 million in a Series C round, while fintech Fasset secured $68 million in its own Series C financing. Together, the transactions brought in $318 million, highlighting the continued availability of large funding commitments for more mature businesses.

Early-stage investment remained comparatively active, with 29 startups securing $86.5 million. Debt financing accounted for $68 million across three transactions, while another seven startups did not disclose their funding stages.

The UAE's performance reflected continued investor appetite for established businesses, even as overall funding declined from the previous quarter.

Yet the reliance on a limited number of large transactions also exposed the uneven nature of the recovery. Excluding Moove and Fasset, UAE startups attracted just $189 million during the quarter, illustrating the extent to which individual deals shaped the country's funding performance.

Egypt struggles to regain momentum

Egypt remained the region's third-largest startup funding market, but investment activity continued to weaken as startups grappled with constrained access to capital and a shortage of sizable financing rounds.

Egyptian startups raised $56.4 million across 15 transactions during the third quarter, down 22% from the $72.6 million recorded in Q2.

The country's quarterly performance was heavily dependent on a single transaction.

Payments infrastructure provider Paymob secured $35 million in a pre-Series C round, accounting for approximately 62% of all capital raised by Egyptian startups during the period.

Without Paymob's financing, Egypt's quarterly total would have fallen to just $21.4 million, underscoring the limited availability of substantial funding for other companies.

Fintech remained the country's leading investment sector, attracting $45 million across two transactions. Edtech ranked second with $3 million raised through one deal, followed by e-commerce infrastructure, which secured $2.8 million in a single transaction.

Early-stage startups accounted for the majority of deal activity, with 10 companies raising a combined $19.3 million.

Paymob's transaction was the country's only later-stage financing round, while debt funding accounted for $1 million across one deal. Another three startups did not disclose their funding stages.

Egypt's continued slowdown reflected a more challenging investment environment, with limited capital availability and fewer large transactions weighing on the country's quarterly performance.

A strong rebound, but not yet a broad recovery

The third-quarter rebound pushed MENA startup funding to approximately $3.4 billion in the first nine months of 2026, providing renewed momentum after a difficult first half marked by geopolitical instability and increasingly selective investment activity.
